cycles.job: X holds case UPDATE, waits W's uncommitted unique job id; W holds that id, waits case KEY SHARE in jobs.case_id FK. J/J cases and J/J jobs are opposite victims of the same cycle.
cycles.stream: X holds case UPDATE, waits W's uncommitted stream; W holds stream, then waits case KEY SHARE in the later jobs INSERT. J/O contexts are opposite victims of the same cycle; streams have no cases FK themselves.
cycles.queued: R holds case SHARE and waits W's unique job/stream; C waits R's transaction for case UPDATE while retaining the tuple-queue position; W holds job/stream and its late FK waits behind C. Same inversion with an extra case-lock waiter, not a separate cause.
